heading: INT. GRAND HOTEL MUSEUM OF CLOCKS - HALL OF PENDULUMS - EVENING

units.text: INT. GRAND HOTEL MUSEUM OF CLOCKS - HALL OF PENDULUMS - EVENING
A cavernous gallery lined with grandfather clocks, their brass pendulums swinging out of step with one another like a crowd of mourners nodding at different tunes.
The parquet gleams.
Tall windows frame a bruised sunset.
Gathered at the center beneath a crystal chandelier: INSPECTOR AUGUSTINE FELL (50s, trench coat damp at the shoulders, fedora in hand), a methodical man with a notebook the size of a prayer book.
MRS. ODETTE LAMBERT-VANCE (60s, pearls, a black veil pushed back), the widow of the museum's founder, perched on a gilt chair.
DR. SIMEON ACHTERBERG (40s, bow tie, spectacles), the curator, nervously winding his own watch.
MISS CLARISSA BOONE (20s, secretary, red lipstick, a pencil behind her ear).
ELIAS THORNCROFT (30s, dark suit, an easy grin), the nephew and heir.
HOBBS (70s, white gloves, spine straight as a ruler), the butler.
Thank you all for staying. It's a nasty night, and I'd hoped we'd be finished by supper.
units.name: FELL

units.text: My husband is lying in the next room, Inspector. Supper is not a priority.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Of course. Forgive me.
units.name: FELL

units.text: The Regulator clock stopped at seven-forty. That's the time on the coroner's slip, isn't it?
units.name: SIMEON

units.text: So it is.
units.name: FELL

units.text: Then he died at seven-forty. It's simple.
units.name: CLARISSA

units.text: It is, Miss Boone. Which is why I distrust it.
units.name: FELL

units.text: Distrust a stopped clock? Inspector, you're a romantic.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: I distrust any clock that stops precisely when it's useful.
units.name: FELL

units.text: If I may, sir.
units.name: HOBBS

units.text: Please.
units.name: FELL

units.text: The Regulator has not stopped on its own in thirty-one years. Mr. Lambert-Vance wound it every Sunday himself. He had a ritual. A key kept on a chain.
units.name: HOBBS

units.text: And that key is now where?
units.name: FELL

units.text: It was in his waistcoat pocket, sir.
units.name: HOBBS

units.text: It was not. I checked.
units.name: FELL

units.text: A pendulum clicks.
Nobody breathes.
What are you suggesting?
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: That someone wound the clock back to seven-forty so that someone else might have an alibi.
units.name: FELL

units.text: I was in the library with Clarissa from seven-fifteen.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Yes. Yes, we were.
units.name: CLARISSA

units.text: You were. And Dr. Achterberg was in the cellar, and Hobbs was serving tea in the east wing, and Madame Lambert-Vance was dressing. Every person in this room has an alibi for seven-forty, which is why I believe the murder occurred at seven-ten.
units.name: FELL

units.text: That's impossible. The tea service was at seven.
units.name: SIMEON

units.text: And ended at seven-oh-five. Hobbs, how many cups did you collect?
units.name: FELL

units.text: Five, sir.
units.name: HOBBS

units.text: There are six people in this house.
units.name: FELL

units.text: A long pause.
The chandelier trembles.
My husband did not take tea after six.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: No. But someone took tea to him. And left the sixth cup upstairs, with lipstick on the rim.
units.name: FELL

units.text: All eyes turn to Clarissa.
She touches her mouth.
Smiles, without joy.
